question: Does Rule30 admit a nontrivial finite-group spatial Lax cocycle with identity vacuum, using block weights of length w and temporal transport of length w+1?
equation: L(F(input))[w bits] * M(input prefix w+1) = M(input suffix w+1) * L(input central w bits), for every input word of length w+2
prize_bridge: Such a law would preserve the conjugacy class of finite spatial monodromy. This is outside additive-density invariants, but existence alone does NOT imply singleton aperiodicity; a seed-specific boundary argument would still be required.
normalization: L(allzero)=identity. Local gauge on de Bruijn vertices of length w-1 fixes a spanning tree of L edges to identity. The allones input equation forces L(allones)=identity. All other L labels are enumerated. All temporal root labels M(zeros) remain allowed.
nontriviality: At least one gauge-normalized L edge is nonidentity. If all L are identity, the spatial product carries no information.
solver: Exact finite-group table enumeration with conjugator-bitset intersections; no SAT solver or installs
positive_verification: Recover all M labels and check all 2^(w+2) original equations independently; demonstrate a nonidentity closed spatial product. Then inspect the actual singleton consequence before making any prize claim.
negative_scope: Only the specified groups, block widths, identity vacuum and local temporal transport. Larger groups, unbounded/spectral groups, nonidentity vacuum, more memory and genuinely nonlocal laws remain open.
timeout: Record partial enumeration, never infer nonexistence from a timeout. No automatic width extension.
